papers.title_en: World Dreamer v5-lite: A Multi-Robot World Action Model with One Dreamer
papers.authors: Guoning Wu, Zijian Cai, Yuhang Zhang, Ying Liu, Yongbin Zheng
papers.evidence: 共享世界状态的多机器人世界动作模型用于环境表示
papers.tldr: 多机器人控制需要融合分布式相机视角并为每个机器人预测独立动作，而现有视觉-语言-动作与世界动作模型多面向单机器人，简单拼接多视角也无法建立空间对应。World Dreamer v5-lite 以共享世界状态为核心：预训练视频编码器的标定特征按工作区坐标填充该状态，空间尺寸不随视角增加而变；VLM 提供场景上下文并为每个机器人给出一个查询，查询读取共享状态并交换位姿感知信息，动作流彼此独立，配合遮蔽视角的协同训练。在 RoboFactory 上平均成功率达 74.0%，超出最强基线 23.7 个百分点；四项真实机器人任务达 78.8%，领先 13.8 点；RoboCasa365 上为 58.08%。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-robot control requires integrating distributed camera views while predicting separate action sequences. Most vision-language-action and world-action models target one robot. Combining multiple views alone does not establish spatial correspondence between them. World Dreamer v5-lite is a multi-robot world-action model built around a shared world state for robot-specific action prediction. Calibrated features from a pretrained video encoder populate this state in workspace coordinates; its spatial size remains fixed as views are added. A vision-language model provides scene context and one query per robot. The queries read the shared state and exchange pose-aware information, while their action streams remain separate. Masked-view cooperative training withholds selected camera views from both visual branches while retaining all action targets. This encourages the use of observations shared by other robots. Pretraining uses more than 10,000 hours of trajectories from 20 simulated robot types, RoboFactory, and real robots. On RoboFactory, World Dreamer v5-lite achieves 74.0% mean success, 23.7 percentage points above the strongest evaluated baseline. Across four real-robot tasks, it reaches 78.8% mean success, a margin of 13.8 points. It also reaches 58.08% overall on RoboCasa365.

papers.title_en: A Hyper-Logical View on Multi-Agent Path Planning
papers.evidence: 用HyperLTL时序逻辑统一刻画多种多智能体路径规划变体
papers.tldr: 多智能体路径规划（MAPP）需为多个智能体生成无碰撞路径，且变体众多、常需各自算法。本文从规格中心视角出发，用HyperLTL及其omega正则扩展HyperQPTL统一建模多种MAPP变体。该视角并非替代专用求解器，而是提供比较变体、添加跨智能体约束和表达最优性的统一语言。它还将MAPP与超属性的验证、解释和因果分析技术相连。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-Agent Path Planning (MAPP) requires collision-free paths for multiple agents. MAPP has numerous real-life applications, including the navigation of automated vehicles, and has therefore many variants considering different constraints, requirements, and objectives. For each such variant, a new algorithmic treatment is often developed. This paper takes a complementary, specification-centered view: we show that many MAPP variants can be modeled in HyperLTL, a temporal logic that reasons about multiple paths and their evolution through time, and in its omega-regular extension HyperQPTL. The contribution is not a claim that current hyperproperty model checkers replace specialized MAPP solvers. Rather, the hyper-logical view gives a unified language for comparing MAPP variants, adding cross-agent constraints, expressing optimality, and connecting MAPP to verification, explanation, and causality techniques for hyperproperties.

papers.title_en: cuArms: GPU-Accelerated Conflict-Based Planning for Multi-Arm Manipulation
papers.authors: Philip Huang, Fabio Ramos, Jiaoyang Li, Caelan Garrett, Lars Johannsmeier
papers.evidence: GPU加速冲突式规划协调多机械臂协作
papers.tldr: 多机械臂操作可提升吞吐与灵巧性，但现有任务分配、调度与联合运动规划方法速度慢、依赖领域假设且扩展性差。cuArms 将冲突搜索与 GPU 并行结合，用可复用多模态路线图分解单臂搜索空间，并以惰性搜索解决冲突和死锁。它再接入高层调度器，把候选任务骨架落地为协调操作计划。实验在仿真和真实工业任务中取得实时初始解与 anytime 改进，刷新多臂规划水平。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-arm manipulation has the potential to dramatically improve the throughput, efficiency, and dexterity of many manipulation tasks. Recent work coordinates multiple robot arms in a shared workcell by allocating and scheduling tasks for greater parallelism, jointly planning multi-arm motions, or directly learning multi-arm policies. So far, these approaches are either too slow, rely on domain-specific assumptions, or scale poorly with the number of robots and task horizon. Thus, we introduce cuArms, a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism that efficiently decomposes the search space using reusable multi-modal roadmaps for individual robots and resolves conflicts and deadlocks through a lazy search. To jointly optimize task assignment, schedules, motions, and manipulation skills, we integrate a high-level scheduler that proposes candidate skeletons for cuArms to ground into coordinated manipulation plans. Experimental results show that our method establishes a new state of the art, with real-time initial solutions and anytime improvements in both motion quality and scheduling, without days of domain-specific training required by learning approaches. Videos of both simulated and real-world industrial tasks are available on https://cuarms.github.io/.

papers.title_en: Repulsive Population Policy Gradients for Behaviorally Diverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Saeed Hedayatian, Harsh Shah, Celine Mneimneh, Stefanos Nikolaidis
papers.evidence: 质量多样性强化学习，优化行为多样的高质量策略种群
papers.tldr: 质量多样性强化学习需找到多样且高性能的策略，但现有方法依赖进化算子，规模扩展成本高。RePPO将PPO用于联合优化紧凑策略种群，以依赖种群、动态塑形的奖励促进策略间排斥与行为多样。连续控制任务上实现较好的质量-多样性权衡，像素输入下保持PPO级质量并显著提升多样性。该工作还首次将QD-RL扩展到LLM微调，为大规模种群优化提供可扩展路径。
papers.abstract_en: The goal of Quality-Diversity Reinforcement Learning (QD-RL) is to find a population of high-performing policies that solve a decision-making problem in diverse ways. Despite recent progress, QD-RL methods predominantly rely on evolutionary operators--including black-box optimizers, mutations, and crossovers--to facilitate exploration and induce diversity. Scaling these methods becomes increasingly costly as policies and behavior spaces grow larger. Building on the Soft QD view of quality-diversity optimization, we introduce \textbf{Re}pulsive \textbf{P}opulation \textbf{P}olicy \textbf{O}ptimization (\textbf{RePPO}), which adapts PPO to jointly optimize a compact population of diverse, high-quality policies using a population-dependent, dynamically shaped reward. On standard continuous-control tasks, RePPO achieves a strong quality-diversity tradeoff compared with state-of-the-art QD-RL methods. Ablations further characterize this tradeoff by examining how each component affects individual quality and collective diversity. To assess RePPO's scalability, we extend our evaluation to learning from pixels and fine-tuning large language models. In pixel-based tasks, where large policies make most traditional QD-RL methods infeasible, RePPO maintains quality on par with standard PPO while achieving substantially higher diversity. Its successful application to language model fine-tuning further demonstrates, for the first time, that QD-RL methods can scale to this domain. Together, these results show that directly optimizing compact populations with RePPO provides a scalable approach to QD-RL across increasingly complex domains.
